title: Make KubernetesPodOperator event logging best-effort and optional
body:
closes: #75013

Since cncf.kubernetes 10.6.0, synchronous pod startup watches Kubernetes events, and repeated API errors could fail a task even after its pod started. This PR makes startup event watching best-effort, so a watcher failure only logs a warning, and adds `log_events_on_startup` to let users disable it.
The docs explain the API server cost and how to opt out. GKE and EKS operators honor the flag in synchronous mode.

<details><summary>AI Summary></summary>

Since cncf.kubernetes 10.6.0 the synchronous `KubernetesPodOperator` polls the Kubernetes events of the pod while it waits for the pod to start. On a large cluster each of those LISTs makes the API server read every event of the namespace from etcd (kube-apiserver keeps no watch cache for `Event` objects), the request times out with 504, and once the client retries were exhausted the failed watcher task was re-raised from `await_pod_start` and failed the task although the pod had started normally. There was no way to switch the watcher off.

This PR:

- makes the sync and async startup event watchers best-effort: an API error that survives the retries logs one warning and stops the watch, while pod start tracking and the task outcome stay unaffected;
- adds `log_events_on_startup` (default `True`) to `KubernetesPodOperator`, `KubernetesPodTrigger` and the `@task.kubernetes` / `@task.kubernetes_cmd` stubs so the watcher can be disabled without subclassing. The trigger serializes the key only when it is `False`, so trigger subclasses with a fixed `__init__` signature (the Amazon `EksPodTrigger`) and triggerers on an older provider keep working;
- documents the behaviour, its cost on the API server and the opt-out.

`GKEStartPodOperator` and `EksPodOperator` honour the flag in synchronous mode only. Forwarding it to their own deferrable triggers needs cncf version floors in the google and amazon providers and is tracked in #75014.

Verified against a local Kubernetes 1.36.1 cluster (docker-desktop): with the events API raising 504 the pod start is still tracked and the task continues, and with the flag off no event LIST is issued.

Checks run locally: `prek run --from-ref upstream/main --stage pre-commit` and `--stage manual` (UI and skill-eval hooks skipped) pass, including `mypy-providers`; the full `providers/cncf/kubernetes/tests/unit` suite passes on sqlite except four pre-existing timezone-dependent `since_time` tests that also fail on `main` unless `TZ=UTC`; the Amazon `EksPodTrigger` tests (4) and the google GKE trigger/operator tests (142) pass.
</details>

     k.dry_run()
 
+Pod events in the task log
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+While the operator waits for the pod to leave the ``Pending`` phase, it reads the Kubernetes events of the pod
+(polling every ``startup_check_interval_seconds`` in synchronous mode) and writes them to the task log
+(scheduling, image pull, container start, and warnings such as ``FailedScheduling``). This logging is
+best-effort: if the events API fails, the operator logs one warning, stops reading events, and the task
+continues.
+
+In synchronous mode each poll is a ``list`` of ``Event`` objects with a field selector. Deferrable
+mode keeps a watch open instead, which costs less but still makes the API server read the namespace
+events each time the watch (re)starts before the first event was seen. The Kubernetes API server
+disables its watch cache for ``Event`` objects by default, so every list is an ``etcd`` read of all
+events in the namespace that is filtered afterwards. On clusters that run thousands of short-lived
+pods in one namespace this adds noticeable API server load.
+Keeping unrelated high-churn pods (for example Spark executors) in a separate namespace reduces the cost.
+
+To turn it off, set ``log_events_on_startup=False``. The parameter is honoured by ``KubernetesPodOperator``,
+``KubernetesPodTrigger``, ``@task.kubernetes`` and ``@task.kubernetes_cmd``. In deferrable mode the opt-out
+is sent to the trigger, so the triggerer needs a provider version that knows the parameter. ``GKEStartPodOperator`` and
+``EksPodOperator`` apply it in synchronous mode only; in deferrable mode their own triggers do not receive
+it yet. It is separate from ``log_events_on_failure``, which controls the one-shot read of events after a
+failure.
+
+.. Forwarding the parameter to the GKE and EKS triggers is tracked at
+   https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/75014
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+    KubernetesPodOperator(
+        task_id="no_startup_events",
+        name="no-startup-events",
+        namespace="default",
+        image="debian",
+        log_events_on_startup=False,
+    )
+
